why_trail.why: Handoff verified complete (task, intent, scope, exclusions, evidence, test mode, stop conditions all present). Both defects reproduced against unmodified HEAD 42df99fd before any fix: the worktree test fails in a detached foreign checkout with the exact hardcoded-path mismatch the handoff described; close_work raises on a work area carrying a gitignored top-level file (mcp_calls.jsonl) and leaves the work area split across two directories with no rollback, exactly as C3 reported. Evidence recorded in BASELINE.md.

Fixed the test: work id is now derived from the checkout's own directory name (ROOT.name) rather than the hardcoded literal "epic-559/c3-lifecycle" -- worktree_path_for only ever looks at the last segment, so this holds for any worktree following the <wt_root>/<work-slug> convention, not just one archived worktree. Added an explicit skip (naming why and where it's reachable) for checkouts outside that convention. The gate's c2 check (grep for the literal anywhere in the file) also caught three UNRELATED pure-function example tests (TestWorktreePathFor, TestBranchNameFor, TestArchiveNameFor) using that same literal as generic sample data, plus a module-docstring path reference that had gone stale after C3's work area was archived -- updated the docstring to the real archived path and swapped the unrelated tests to a different sample work id (same coverage, no behavior change). tests/test_spine_lifecycle.py passes in full (53 passed) in this worktree.

close_work now classifies each top-level entry (tracked / untracked-not-ignored / untracked-and-ignored via git check-ignore) and moves the untracked-ignored case on the filesystem directly, since git add refuses an untracked ignored path outright -- this is exactly the mcp_calls.jsonl/mcp_server_started shape the MCP door leaves behind. The "everything else" batch is wrapped: a failure partway through restores every already-moved entry (including a filesystem-moved ignored one and a partially-staged git rename) before the exception propagates, so the work area is never left split. Spine-last stays deliberately OUTSIDE that rollback wrapping: a failure at that already-last step still leaves spine and journal at their original, retryable path -- unchanged, still covered by the existing TestCloseWorkSpineLastUnderInterruption / TestCloseWorkDifferingBasenameMandatory tests, both still green. New fixture (_make_work_area with ignored_file=) builds a work area carrying a gitignored file via a real, committed .gitignore. RED observed and FALSIFIED both attested with the mutation experiment (c2). Full suite: 2934 passed, 3 skipped, 1121 subtests (baseline was 2932; +2 for the two new tests).
